newsitem.title: USA: PS Enterprise reorganizes unregulated units.
newsitem.headline: PS Enterprise reorganizes unregulated units.

text.p: Public Service Enterprise Group Inc said on Wednesday that it is reorganizing its unregulated activities following the retirement of two key executives.
In addition, the company said, the changes will result in a clearer division between Enterprise's regulated and unregulated businesses and increase efficiencies.
Among other things, the chief operating officer of its regulated utility, Lawrence R. Codey, will take on the responsibility for electric and natural gas wholesale sales.
These are sales to utilities and brokers with the revenues credited to Public Service Electric & Co.

The company said Paul H. Way, president of Enterprise Diversified Holdings Inc and Arthur S. Nislick, president of Community Energy Alternatives Inc, Enterprise's independent power production business, are retiring.

PS Enterprise said Robert J. Dougherty Jr, was named to succeed Way and head up an expanded EDHI as its president and chief operating officer. He had been president and chief operating officer of Enterprise Ventures & Services Corp.

In addition to continuing to oversee U.S. Energy Partners, Enterprise Strategic Energy Solutions and the two way customer communication initiative, Dougherty will manage and develop Enterprise subsidiaries in non-regulated areas.
Michael J. Thomson was named president of CEA, succeeding Nislick and reporting to Dougherty. He previously had been CEA's chief operating officer.

PS Enterprise said Frank Cassidy will become chief executive of a yet unnamed subsidiary, including the company's unregulated energy services activities with the mandate to consolidate several existing subsidiaries.
Cassidy had been senior vice president, Fossil Generation, at PSE&G. He will report to Dougherty.
Pat Colgan, currently director, Load Following Generation, was named named to succeed Cassidy at the utility.
